subject: GPU ramp bridge request — Orion Edge
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: GPU ramp bridge request — Orion Edge

Ben / Marissa,

Heads-up on a late-stage opportunity with Orion Edge (ARN: ORN-2026-431). They want a 12-week pilot starting nominally in early January, with an anticipated production ramp by March. Quick summary of expected sizing (attached):
- Week 1–2: 8 nodes (approx 10 T4-equivalent GPUs) for evaluation
- Week 3–8 (pilot steady state): 16 nodes (approx 20 GPUs)
- Peak burst during model validation weeks 9–12: additional 20 GPUs (total ~40)

They're asking for a short provisional hold so procurement doesn't get blocked if we hit capacity crunch in winter. Can ops confirm:
1) Available GPU pool in us-west for Jan–Mar (per week granularity)
2) Whether we can offer a 14-day provisional hold (soft) of ~20 GPUs while they finalize PO and SOC paperwork
3) Any maintenance windows or scheduled capacity events that would affect coverage

Attached: MVP_workload_estimates.xlsx (per-week load), redwood-dedicated-sla-summary.pdf

Goal: get a provisional hold and an ETA on firm availability so I can commit next steps with their procurement lead.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T10:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: GPU ramp bridge request — Orion Edge

Jordan,

Thanks for the context and the workbook — good detail. Quick initial read:
- Current free pool (us-west, general-purpose) shows ~120 GPUs available across our Dedicated clusters as of this morning.
- Reservations already committed for Jan–Mar reduce usable headroom; after accounting for committed Dedicated capacity, we have ~60 GPUs that are not otherwise reserved.

A few clarifying asks before we put anything on soft hold:
- Can you confirm whether Orion requires a particular SKU (A100 vs A30 vs T4) or if they accept compatible fallback variants?
- Do they need strict colocation (same AZ) for latency-sensitive workloads?

We can do a provisional soft hold of up to 20 GPUs for 14 days while you push procurement, but we need the following to lock it in:
- Owner (sales SLA) who will confirm PO date within the 14 days
- An explicit fallback policy (if PO isn't received, GPUs released automatically)

Notes / constraints:
- We have a scheduled cluster upgrade in us-west on 2026-01-10 that may temporarily reduce burst capacity for 24 hours.
- If they insist on A100-only, available A100 inventory is tighter (~18 GPUs free today).

If you're ok, I'll place a provisional hold for 20 GPUs today and mark the hold as expiring 2026-12-06 unless we get a PO or extend it. Also looping Markus for capacity planning and Stephanie for deal coordination.

Cheers,

Ben Carter
Capacity Operations Lead | Redwood Inference
[ben.carter@redwood.com]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@orion-edge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: GPU ramp bridge request — Orion Edge

Samir,

Forwarding the capacity read from our ops team (below). Attached are the workload estimates and a short SLA summary for Dedicated capacity. High level ask from our side: would you be comfortable with an initial provisional soft hold (~20 GPUs) while your procurement team finalizes the PO? That hold would only be for 14 days and would give you the headroom to avoid losing the window in January.

Quick reminder of the timeline we discussed on the call: pilot kickoff early January -> pilot run 6–8 weeks -> production ramp by March. For the pilot they indicated they only need ~10 GPUs for the first two weeks, then scale to ~20. If that matches your expectations, let me know and I'll ask ops to put the soft hold in place.

Best,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]

From: Samir Patel <samir@orion-edge.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Orion Edge Procurement <procurement@orion-edge.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: GPU ramp bridge request — Orion Edge

Jordan — thanks for the update and for pushing on capacity. A few quick answers from our side:
- SKU: for the pilot we're fine with A30-equivalent; production may prefer A100 for some validation runs but not strictly required day one.
- Colocation: prefer same AZ for the pilot, but only if it doesn't materially delay the start.
- Procurement: I'm looping our procurement contact here (procurement@orion-edge.ai). They'll need the following to push the PO in the next 10 business days:
  - Formal quote and PO-ready invoice
  - SOC2 evidence (we have a copy from initial security email but procurement will re-request)

If Redwood can place a 14-day soft hold, that will give us time to confirm internal approvals. For the pilot we can commit to 10 GPUs immediately and provide a PO within 7–10 business days. If that works, please proceed.

Thanks,

Samir Patel
VP Product | Orion Edge
[samir@orion-edge.ai]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T15:48:00-08:00
Subject: RE: GPU ramp bridge request — Orion Edge

Jordan / team,

Per Samir's reply we can be flexible on SKU (A30 ok for the pilot). I've placed a provisional soft hold for 16 GPUs in us-west (AZ-a preferred) with an expiration of 2026-12-06 — rationale: pilot asks for 10, allow buffer for validation bursts.

Action items captured:
- Ops: soft hold placed (16 GPUs) – will flag on our capacity board and push an alert if usage approaches 80% of remaining pool.
- Sales (Jordan): get PO within 14 days or request extension via marissa.cole@redwood.com.
- Security: Marissa to share SOC2 evidence directly with procurement@orion-edge.ai (see attached).

Fallback plan: if PO not received by 2026-12-06, hold auto-releases. If Orion requests A100-only and we can't secure 16 A100s, we'll offer split (A30 for pilot, A100 for validation windows) and list out migration steps.

Linking HubSpot deal for visibility: https://hubspot.com/deals/ORN-2026-431

Ben Carter
Capacity Operations Lead | Redwood Inference
